title: Financial statement analysis
audience: a college student in a finance, accounting or business degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Analyze profitability, efficiency, liquidity and solvency with ratios and DuPont analysis, assess earnings and cash-flow quality, adjust statements for comparability, analyze segments, and build a simple forecast of the statements.
primary_reading: MIT OpenCourseWare 15.535 Business Analysis Using Financial Statements (free)

weeks.1: The analysis framework and sources of information
weeks.9: Analyzing inventories, long-lived assets and leases

blocks.deliverable: Prepare common-size statements for two companies.
Assess a company's ability to pay its debts.
Week 7 midterm; find the warning signs in a case company.
Adjust two companies' statements to be comparable.
Forecast an income statement and balance sheet one year ahead.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Company analysis: pick a public company and its main competitor, analyze five years of statements with ratios, DuPont and cash flow analysis, assess earnings quality, forecast next year, and write a four-page analyst report with a supported conclusion.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
